meta.label: Loop

meta.label: Mute

meta.label: Delete
meta.click: Nothing: a modifier only [RemoteFM1; Move deletes the clip]
meta.hold: Its mark (scissors) at the press. + a step with notes: cut, crossed. + an empty step: the clipboard pasted. + any step right after a cut: pasted over it. + pad: that note out of the clip [M]. + encoder: its automation [M]. + Play: the clip cleared. + wheel press: the device. + track button: the track cleared
meta.description: One clipboard with Copy; a paste never empties it. Back clears the marks.

meta.label: Copy

meta.hold: Its mark (two sheets) at the press. + a step with notes: copied, dashed; several: a group. + an empty step: pasted. Let go after copying, then a step: pasted once [M]. + wheel press: the device. + track button: the track
meta.description: Copy never overwrites a full step.

meta.label: Undo

meta.hold: The list of recent actions; the wheel picks how far back [Melodee]

meta.label: Shift

meta.label: Left

meta.label: Right

items.text: LOOP MODE: PAGES. Loop, quick click: latched. The steps are the clip's pages, up to 16, as Move's bars [12.1] with RemoteFM1's page edit: the wheel is the length, and the two lower pad rows set where the last page ends. Here 4 pages, the last ending after 5 steps: 53 steps.

items.text: NOTE MODE: CHORDS LAYOUT. ChoralRoot's Move layout as a pad layout. Top left: chord types (violet) and extensions (orange); here MIN and m7 are held. Top right: eight chord pads (teal). Below: the roots, one octave of the Keyboard layout; D is down, so D minor seven sounds. The encoders are the PADS page.

items.name: Note Mode: Progression layout
items.description: A Ripchord-style progression on the two-octave Keyboard layout: every key plays the chord stored on it. Each chord stays on the key its pack put it on, so the main chords are on the white keys and the accents on the black keys. Here Em7 sounds. The encoders are the PADS page.

items.text: NOTE MODE: PROGRESSION LAYOUT. A Ripchord-style progression on the two-octave Keyboard layout: every key plays the chord stored on it. Each chord stays on the key its pack put it on, so the main chords are on the white keys and the accents on the black keys. Here Em7 sounds. The encoders are the PADS page.

items.name: Inside a device: the map row
items.description: Inside the synth, on its FILTER page, with the map row on (MOD side). The top row of pads is the synth's sources; LFO 1 is held and the Cutoff encoder is turning, so LFO 1 now moves Cutoff by +40. The three rows under it still play. After Serum; EvilGenius on the Move maps the same way.

items.name: A picker belt
items.description: Where the wheel chooses one of several kinds of thing, the kinds ride a conveyor as boxes of pixel art, after EvilGenius: the chosen one large in the middle, its name large under the belt. Here the pad layouts of Shift + Step 8. A turn moves the belt a box; a press takes the one in the middle.

items.name: Session Mode's belt
items.description: The wheel touched or turned in Session Mode: the mixer's pages (SCOPES, LEVEL, PAN, SEND A, SEND B), then each bus's effects, riding into OUT at the right. A page is live as it reaches the middle; an effect is entered with a press. Let go, and the screen goes back to the meters.

items.name: A device page at rest
items.description: Inside a device: its page as eight pictograms, two rows of four as the encoders lie, each drawing its own value, with no words. The page's name large. The strip: a square for the device's preset, then a segment a page.

items.name: An encoder touched or turned
items.description: The touched parameter takes the screen: its name, its value as the largest thing, its unit, and eight marks showing which encoder it is. It stays for a second after the encoder is let go.

items.name: The wheel touched
items.description: Where you are, in words: track, device, page and its place. With Speech on Jog this is also said.

items.name: Copy held
items.description: A held modifier is its picture and its one word. The lights on the surface are the list of what it can act on; the screen does not spell it out.

items.name: A message
items.description: A message takes the whole screen for a second, in at most two large lines.

items.name: A list
items.description: The item under the wheel large, its neighbours small above and below, where the list is at the bottom.

items.name: Saving and loading: the sheet
items.description: A press on a rack's or a device's front item: the preset's name with a mark because it has changed, and the sheet in large type: Load, Save, then Save As, Init and Revert below.

items.name: Projects
items.description: Shift + Step 1: the 32 pads as a grid, the selected slot framed, its name large.

items.name: A device's main page: its theme
items.description: The first page of a device after its name: its own weird world, full screen, with its eight key parameters on the encoders. A sketch for a delay: a canyon and a ball. Time is how far apart it lands, feedback how many times it bounces, the filter on the repeats the fog it bounces into. No words: a touch names a parameter. The strip: the device's name, then this page, then its plain pages.

items.name: View: a scene
items.description: A track's rest picture can be its instrument's scene, after the h1 firmware: here a pond at night. Each note is a fish that jumps where its pitch puts it and leaves ripples; a macro raises the moon. No words.

items.name: View: Scope
items.description: The track's sound as one waveform across the screen, held still on its pitch. Inside a device it is the sound as it leaves that device.

items.name: View: Scope 8
items.description: All eight tracks' waveforms, two rows of four as the encoders lie: the selected track's framed, a muted one dotted, a silent one flat.

items.name: View: Tracks
items.description: The four tracks of the bank, a row each in the order of the track buttons, each its own page and playhead. The track's number large at the left, the selected one boxed.

items.text:
FEVERDREAM, DRAFT 1. See docs/DESIGN.md.

1. Move first: every gesture in the Move manual does the same here. [M] in a control's notes marks it.
2. New things use Move's three shapes: select then turn; hold a thing then turn; modifier plus target.
3. The picture says where you are, a touch says what a control does, a message what just happened.
4. A held modifier shows a hint card and lights its targets amber.
6. Two hands, never three: Note/Session held is a second Shift under the left thumb.
7. Everything can be said: a screen reader from the first screen (Schwung's voice). Speech: Off, On, or Jog (only while the wheel is touched). Every view, popup, value and change has words.
PRESSES: quick click = released inside the 300 ms hold window; hold = still down when it ends; double click. A button with a hold feature shows nothing before the hold and does its quick click on release.
5. No hidden modes: a lit button and a symbol in the screen's corner for every state.
8. Big, simple, told on touch: the screen is small, so nothing depends on small text. Three sizes of type, three lines at most.

LED colours keep Move's meanings: white selected / notes, track colour exists, green playing, red recording and automation, pink sampling, blue solo. Amber is new: a modifier's targets.

EIGHT TRACKS, FOUR BUTTONS. Bank A = tracks 1-4, bank B = 5-8. Shift + a track button: the same row in the other bank. The track's number is boxed on the screen. Colours run warm (A) to cool (B).

DEVICES, AS IN LIVE: RACK | MACROS | PADS · SEQ · MIDI effects · INSTRUMENT · audio effects · MIX. SAVE AND LOAD: a rack's or a device's name stands at its front; a press on it opens one sheet (Load, Save, Save As, Init, Revert). The wheel walks the chain, a press enters a device, Back leaves; Shift + wheel moves a device inside its zone; at the chain the encoders are the track's macros (banks of 8). Every device: 8 values a page, a face, presets, locks.

SENDS AND MASTER are chains too, in Session Mode on the wheel, where Move has its main effects.

SESSION: columns are tracks, rows are scenes (decided 23 Nov 2026). All 8 tracks on the pads; the track buttons launch scenes; two steps under each column select and stop the track.
